A_target.statement:
Let $P_0, P_1, \ldots, P_n \in \R^d$ be [[Definition:Control Point|control points]].
Let:
:$\displaystyle \map B t = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \binom n k t^k \paren {1 - t}^{n - k} P_k$
be the [[Definition:Bézier Curve|Bézier curve]].
Then $B$ is the [[Definition:Limit of Sequence|limit]] of repeated [[Definition:Subdivision (Bézier Curve)|subdivision]] of its control polygon, and $\map B t$ lies in the [[Definition:Convex Hull|convex hull]] of $\set {P_0, \ldots, P_n}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $Q$ be a [[Definition:Polygon|polygon]].
[[Definition:Corner Cutting|Cutting a corner]] at a [[Definition:Vertex of Polygon|vertex]] $V$ replaces $V$ with two points on its adjacent edges, each an [[Definition:Convex Combination|interpolation]] of the endpoints of that edge.

substitutions.the polygon whose corners are cut: the control polygon of the curve
substitutions.the sequence of refined polygons: successive subdivisions converging to the curve

derived.each refined polygon lying in the previo: the curve lies in the convex hull of the control points

object_map.reformulation: Replace the smooth curve by a polygon and refine it by corner cutting, so the curve becomes a limit of finite data.

validity_conditions: Each corner cut replaces a vertex by points on its adjacent edges, so every refined polygon lies inside the convex hull of the previous one.
The nested convex hulls shrink, and the polygon vertices converge uniformly, so the limit curve exists and lies in the original convex hull.
The limit is the polynomial curve given by the Bernstein basis, which is checked by verifying the subdivision reproduces the de Casteljau recursion.
proof_plan:
Start from the control polygon $P_0 P_1 \cdots P_n$.
Cut corners by the [[De Casteljau's Algorithm|de Casteljau]] scheme at parameter $t$:
:$P_k^{\paren {j + 1} } = \paren {1 - t} P_k^{\paren j} + t P_{k + 1}^{\paren j}$

Each new vertex is a [[Definition:Convex Combination|convex combination]] of the previous vertices.
Hence each refined polygon lies in the [[Definition:Convex Hull|convex hull]] of the previous one.

Iterating the subdivision, the edge lengths of the refined polygons shrink geometrically.
Hence the vertices converge [[Definition:Uniform Convergence|uniformly]] to a limit curve.

By [[Principle of Mathematical Induction|induction]] on $j$:
:$\displaystyle P_0^{\paren n} = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \binom n k t^k \paren {1 - t}^{n - k} P_k = \map B t$
so the limit curve is the polynomial curve in the [[Definition:Bernstein Polynomial|Bernstein basis]].
{{qed}}
